successors.name: Maurya Empire
successors.text: the Nanda state in 322: 'The Nanda dynasty was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya'

ledger.x: 345 BCE: Mahapadma founds the Nanda Empire at Pataliputra.

c. 340 BCE: the Kuru country passes to the Nandas. 'The Greek records suggest that the king of Gangaridai and Prasii controlled this region, which may be taken as corrorobrative evidence for the Nanda conquest of the Kuru territory' (the page's spelling). Undated: the page lists the 'Kurus' among the Kshatriyas…

c. 340 BCE: the Nandas hold Kalinga. 'The inscription states that "Nanda-raja" (the Nanda king) had excavated a canal in Kalinga' and the empire 'appears to have stretched from present-day Punjab in the west to Odisha in the east'. Undated; the page lists the 'Kalingas' among the Kshatriyas Mahapadma is 'said to have'…
333 BCE: the Nanda realm reaches its full extent in Cliopatria.
322 BCE: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the last Nanda king, Dhana Nanda.

wars.name: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory over the kings of the Punjab and the Indus; Alexander's army mutinied at the Hyphasis (Beas) 'refusing to march further east' and never met the Nandas, whose army the page calls 'five times the size of the Macedonian army'.

wars.name: Nanda conquests under Mahapadma
wars.outcome: The Nandas subjugate Pañcāla, Surasena and the Kuru country and the empire reaches 'from present-day Punjab in the west to Odisha in the east'.

wars.name: Chandragupta Maurya's overthrow of the Nandas
wars.outcome: Chandragupta, supported by Chanakya, overthrows the Nanda dynasty (infobox c.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by a text or a survey: the page says the empire 'appears to have stretched' from Punjab to Odisha and that there is 'no concrete evidence' of rule south of the Vindhya.
